mission: Day four in hyperspace. The ship smells like six people in a space for two. Desh keeps an ironic tally of arguments on his datapad. Kael laughs for the first time anyone has heard — short, genuine, cut off. The whole ship notices.
why_now: Breathing room between nodes. The Kael/Desh warmth needs one more visible beat before the midpoint, and Ben and Desh both need the cockpit-door to close on them before Scene 2 can happen.
conflict: Low-level friction from overcrowding. Sera's formality grates against Desh's casualness. Torin's warmth lands on its beats slightly too cleanly — the first time anyone might register the timing as a rhythm rather than a person.
turning_point: Kael laughs. A short, genuine sound, cut short the way Kael cuts everything. The whole ship notices without saying so.
opening_hook: Day four in hyperspace. The ship smells like six people who've been living in a space designed for two. Desh has started keeping score of arguments.
closing_hook: Desh catches Ben alone in the cockpit. 'Can we talk about something that isn't the Force?' His voice is too casual. Whatever he wants to discuss, he's been working up to it.
emotional_trajectory: Cramped humor -> interpersonal warmth (Kael's laugh) -> Desh's deliberate opening

stakes.personal: Kael allowing himself a fraction of company — small but significant
stakes.interpersonal: Group bonds forming through proximity and shared adversity

setting: Aboard the Steady Returns — various locations, hyperspace transit
sensory_details: Recycled air getting stale; Desh's caf supply dwindling; Kael's laugh arriving and leaving before anyone can turn around; Torin telling a story from the NSW with timing that arrives on its beats slightly too cleanly
action_beats: Desh marks another tally on his datapad argument tracker as Sera and Torin disagree about galley rotation
Kael laughs at something Desh says — a short, genuine sound that stops every conversation on the ship
Desh drops into the co-pilot seat beside Ben with studied casualness and waits until the cockpit door closes
notes: Torin's warmth becoming slightly mechanical is the subtlest note in the chapter — plant it in timing, not in Ben's interior analysis. The reader should feel a story that lands too cleanly before anyone has the word for it. Kael's laugh is a single line and a cut; do not describe him smiling at length. Diagnostic-voice trap — Ben should not, in this scene, articulate 'Torin's warmth is becoming a performance' as interiority. He files the mis-fit the way he files the smell of the ship; analysis belongs to later chapters. Voice: Allston-warm throughout. Anti-pattern: no scene-starter atmospherics; open on action, dialogue, or a concrete observation.
